proof_review: The complete L047 transitive classification and L044 exact alternating maxima force the actual group to be Sn above the stated strict threshold. An actual maximal omission is proper and inherits a C-marking by IP. For n>=7 the only above-half transitive possibilities are exactly the odd-block wreath family, the degree-eight rank-five exception, and A11 rank six. Natural Sn itself is excluded because the omission is proper.

The parent Sn noncommutation diagram is connected by actual IP and direct indecomposability. In the wreath case the omission has an isolated constant flip and a noncentral path. Thus the missing mark is next to that isolated mark and one endpoint of the path, not an endpoint of the whole string. This corrects the source argument while retaining its rank strategy.

The complete acquired block proof supplies the actual base vectors lambda and lambda+e1 before its abstract cocycle normalization. Complement lifts are not silently conjugated as permutation actions. At the v endpoint the generic acquired pair-centralizer lemma applies to the actual complement with primitive block image Sm; its regular prime-dihedral exception is impossible. At the other endpoint the conjugates lambda+ej for j<m form a base subgroup nontrivial on every coordinate. Its literal point orbits are the original pairs, so any centralizing permutation preserves that pair partition. Both cases contradict natural Sn.

The S8 argument uses the complete connected rank-six parent census, not a classification of arbitrary lower-rank subgroups. Connectedness was already proved. The two literal representatives and all twelve omissions match the acquired output; every omission is intransitive.

The A11 omission must occur at an endpoint because its own noncommutation diagram is connected by simplicity. The missing mark centralizes the five distant marks. All four acquired rank-six representatives and both orientations have trivial unrestricted centralizer in S11. Appending and fixing a new point computes precisely that unrestricted centralizer, without imposing a hidden anchor condition on the eleven old points.

Once all actual omissions are intransitive, every label has a transposition crossing two omission orbits. A cycle of selected distinct-label edges would give an alternate path in the omission group across its own selected edge. This proves that every selection is a forest.

For n5 and n6 the rank bounds force rank n-1 and the acquired full extremal classification identifies the simplex only up to marked-group isomorphism. Choosing its ordinary adjacent-transposition action gives the conclusion. The outer degree-six tuple has all five omissions transitive in the literal replay; the manuscript claims only that both endpoints are transitive, which is true. It expressly excludes a universal statement about every degree-six permutation action.
